t: For expenses, not otherwise provided for, necessary to meet annual obligations of membership in international multilateral organizations, pursuant to treaties ratified pursuant to the advice and consent of the Senate, conventions or specific Acts of Congress, $1,166,212,000: Provided, That the Secretary of State shall, at the time of the submission of the President’s budget to Congress under section 1105(a) of title 31, United States Code, transmit to the Committees on Appropriations the most recent biennial budget prepared by the United Nations for the operations of the United Nations: Provided further, That the Secretary of State shall notify the Committees on Appropriations at least 15 days in advance (or in an emergency, as far in advance as is practicable) of any United Nations action to increase funding for any United Nations program without identifying an offsetting decrease elsewhere in the United Nations budget and cause the United Nations budget for the biennium 2006–2007 to exceed the revised United Nations budget level for the biennium 2004–2005 of $3,695,480,000: Provided further, That any payment of arrearages under this title shall be directed toward special activities that are mutually agreed upon by the United States and the respective international organization: Provided further, That none of the funds appropriated in this paragraph shall be available for a United States contribution to an international organization for the United States share of interest costs made known to the United States Government by such organization for loans incurred on or after October 1, 1984, through external borrowings.

fable.w: This is an appropriation for dues to international organizations. Its transmittal and 15-day notification requirements run only to the Committees on Appropriations, which are inside the federal government. The tempting reading is that the "mutually agreed upon" clause is coordination with an outside entity, but it is better read as a condition on how arrearage payments are spent, agreed with the recipient of the funds, much like contract or grant terms. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation process or right to sue, though the clause makes this a closer call than the rest of the section.
fable.s: any payment of arrearages under this title shall be directed toward special activities that are mutually agreed upon by the United States and the respective international organization

opus.w: The procedural requirements here are transmissions and notices to the Committees on Appropriations, and Congress is inside the federal government, so they are not participation. The clause directing arrearage payments to activities 'mutually agreed upon by the United States and the respective international organization' sets a negotiated term for how funds are spent between the payer and the recipient. It does not set up an outside party consulting on, commenting on, or challenging a federal policy decision, so the tempting 'Yes' reading fails.
opus.s: the Secretary of State shall notify the Committees on Appropriations at least 15 days in advance (or in an emergency, as far in advance as is practicable) of any United Nations action to increase funding
opus.b: **Reasoning:** The tempting reading is "Yes," because arrearage payments must go to "special activities that are mutually agreed upon by the United States and the respective international organization," and an international organization is outside the federal government. That reading fails on closer look. The mutual agreement is a negotiated term about where U.S. money goes. It works like a funding or treaty arrangement between parties, not a federal agency consulting outsiders before making a policy decision. The other procedural parts of the section don't count either: transmitting the UN budget and notifying the Appropriations Committees are reports to Congress, which is inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of State to notify the Committees on Appropriations (a part of Congress) before certain actions. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Therefore, this notification is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of State shall notify the Committees on Appropriations at least 15 days in advance
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for the Secretary of State to notify the Committees on Appropriations constitutes "participation" because it involves communication with an external body before a decision (payment) is made. However, this fails because Congress and its committees are explicitly defined as being **inside** the federal government. The definition states: "Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government." Therefore, reporting to or notifying Congress is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties.
